title: The lake that sized a world

beats.line: Before there were any people on Kiros, there was a drawing: coastlines and lakes in blue ink.
Kayden wanted to stand inside it, from orbit all the way down to a lakeshore.
But a drawing has no scale. So one lake became the ruler for the whole world.
Lake Veir is sized like Lake Bonneville, the ancient Utah lake: fifty-one thousand square kilometers.
Put that lake on an Earth-sized planet, and the land only reaches nineteen degrees north.
That's all tropics. But the canon has taiga, snowfields and an Ice Sea far to the north.
beats.ssml: That's all tropics. But the canon has taiga, snowfields and an Ice <break time='150ms'/> Sea far to the north.

beats.line: One answer: shrink the planet to about the size of our Moon, seventeen hundred kilometers in radius.
Gravity falls to about a quarter of Earth's. Giant forests and flying dragons start making sense.
A Python pipeline turns the ink into heights. Your browser builds the planet from them.
Then a newer drawing moved Lake Veir four hundred forty kilometers. Which ruler wins is still undecided.
